notes: This is an English handwritten correction list. The top entry is clipped or effaced; no missing phrase has been reconstructed. Page references and line numbers identify material being corrected, not pagination of these notes. There is no visible title or stated page count; the archive corner number is 20.

At p.87 line 8 the writer offers two forms, with have singly underlined in the first. At p.88 line 2 the misplaced apostrophe in does'nt is contrasted with doesn't, with a further remark about is'nt below.

At p.89 line 3, or alternatively introduces to have made me. Line 8 asks whether very is necessary. Line -15 says last but not least is more usual and offers an alternative would be last, not least,. These are alternatives and a question, not categorical replacement commands.

At p.90 line -15 compare and commute take with; the right-side note counts 4 instances on this page. The double-negative remark and not -- neither are locally crossed out. The live isn't reference ends (twice). At line -8 a replacement would give better flow of words.

At p.91 the writer contrasts in view of with with the view to, then discusses we've got, we have got, We got, and a conditional example. The grammatical statements are transcribed without an external grammar check.
At p.92 the suggestion is qualified by probably and points to a repeat at line -3. At p.99 the variable-name change to F, G is qualified by it seems.
The earlier group is crossed by two long oblique lines. Sent 19/12/83 stands at the right above the horizontal rule, after p.100. The later entries below the rule cite pp.102 through 115.

The lower group repeats commute with and contraction corrections; developing is annotated single p.; the p.107 line -3 names and a raised cancelled character remain partly doubtful; the medial s of relationships has two short underline strokes.
